parsed_blocks.text: On Saturday morning Anna makes a shopping list before she goes shopping. She writes down milk, bread, eggs, rice, and jam. Then she walks to the big supermarket near her flat. She checks her list twice before she leaves the house.

Inside the supermarket, food stands in long rows called aisles. Anna cannot find the rice, so she asks a shop assistant for help. 'Excuse me, which aisle is the rice in?' she asks. The assistant tells her the rice is in the next aisle, past the bread. Anna walks down the bread aisle first. She sees the jam on a high shelf above the bread. She takes a jar of jam and puts it in her basket.

Anna only has three things in her basket, so she carries it easily. But her list is long, so she takes a big trolley instead. In the fresh section she chooses apples and fish that came in today. Next to it is the frozen section, where fish and vegetables sit in cold boxes. She keeps the list in her pocket while she shops.

Anna needs water, so she picks a big bottle from the shelf. Next to it is milk in a tall carton. She finds fish in a small tin and rice in a paper packet. She already has jam in a jar from the first aisle.
By the eggs, a sign says special offer. You can get one box free when you buy one. Anna takes two boxes of eggs for the price of one.

Now her trolley is full, so Anna goes to the checkout. Many people wait in the queue before her. When it is her turn, the cashier scans every item quickly. At the end, Anna takes her receipt and puts the shopping in her bag. Anna is happy with her shopping and walks home with a full bag.

data.definition: a long row in a shop between the shelves, where you walk to find things
data.example: Anna walks down the bread aisle first.

data.definition: a flat board in a shop where things stand so you can see and reach them
data.example: She sees the jam on a high shelf above the bread.

data.definition: a big container on wheels that you push around the shop for a lot of shopping; in American English people often say cart
data.example: Her list is long, so she takes a big trolley instead.

data.definition: a small container with a handle that you carry in your hand for just a few things
data.example: She takes a jar of jam and puts it in her basket.

data.definition: not frozen and not old; food that came into the shop only today or yesterday
data.example: In the fresh section she chooses apples and fish that came in today.

data.definition: kept very cold in a special part of the shop so it lasts a long time
data.example: Next to it is the frozen section, where fish and vegetables sit in cold boxes.

data.definition: a tall container made of glass or plastic, used for water, milk, or oil
data.example: Anna picks a big bottle from the shelf.

data.definition: a tall container made of cardboard, used mostly for milk or juice
data.example: Next to it is milk in a tall carton.

data.definition: a small metal container that keeps food like fish for a long time; in American English people often say can
data.example: She finds fish in a small tin.

data.definition: a small container made of glass with a lid, used for jam
data.example: She already has jam in a jar from the first aisle.

data.definition: a container made of paper or thin plastic, used for things like rice
data.example: She finds rice in a paper packet.

data.definition: the place in a shop where you take your basket or trolley to finish shopping; in British shops some people call it the till
data.example: Now her trolley is full, so Anna goes to the checkout.

data.definition: a line of people waiting for their turn; in American English people often say line
data.example: Many people wait in the queue before her.

data.definition: the small paper you get after the checkout, showing what you bought; some people call it a slip
data.example: Anna takes her receipt and puts the shopping in her bag.

data.definition: a paper with the names of the things you plan to buy, that you bring with you to the shop
data.example: On Saturday morning Anna makes a shopping list before she goes shopping.

data.definition: words on a sign next to a product, telling you that it is cheaper today or that you get something extra
data.example: The sign by the eggs says special offer: you can get one box free when you buy one.

data.definition: to move a product's barcode past a machine at the checkout so the price appears
data.example: The cashier scans every item quickly.
